questions.question: Where does a newcomer get the tool's one file, and what kind of script is it? The CCS says the user copies one file into a folder on their PATH, but it gives no address to download the file from and does not say whether the file is a Python 3 script or a POSIX sh script. Without these the README cannot give a download command that works or say what Requirements must be in place (Python 3 or nothing beyond a shell), so the reader cannot install the tool from the README alone.
questions.recommended: Give the public repository address the file will be published at, with the file as a POSIX sh script, since sh is on every macOS and Linux system while Python 3 is sometimes missing on macOS, so Requirements stays at macOS or Linux and a terminal.

questions.question: Which license is tidy-downloads under, and which pages do Documentation (fuller use, what changed in each version) and Development (the entrance to the architecture and development) link to? The CCS and docs/ux.md name none, so the README can neither name the license nor link to places the reader can reach.
questions.recommended: MIT, with Documentation linking to docs/usage.md and CHANGELOG.md and Development linking to docs/architecture.md, each made in this branch before the README is accepted, since MIT is short and common for a small tool and links only count when what they point to is there.
